chunks: And from him, from several of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abdullah ibn Junbud, from Sufyan ibn al-Simṭ, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'When the child reaches four months, perform hijma (cupping) on him every month at the nape of the neck, for it dries up his saliva and brings down the bitterness from his head and body.'
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended Islamic practice for infant health and cupping according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) illustrates the integration of Prophetic medicine (Tibb al-Nabawi) with Shia jurisprudence, specifically addressing the health of children in the context of divorce rulings. It prescribes monthly cupping at the nape (an-nuqrah) to purify the infant’s system by drying saliva and drawing out 'bitterness' (mararah), reflecting the contemporary medical understanding of humoral balance in Shia scholarly tradition.
